items.title: Educational software, not qualification
items.text: This is educational software, not qualification to perform hazardous procedures independently. Use instructor-approved protocols, current SDS information and institutional EHS guidance.

items.title: Personal protective equipment
items.text: Gloves, goggles and a lab coat from set-up to clean-up. Never touch a slide near silver with metal forceps.

items.title: Fume hood
items.text: In the hood: making the ammoniacal silver, the ammonia rinses, the developer, and xylene.

items.title: Xylene (dewaxing)
items.text: Xylene is flammable and toxic to breathe: use it in the hood.

items.title: Silver nitrate
items.text: 20% silver nitrate stains skin and is an oxidizer. Keep it dark and fresh; use plastic forceps.

items.title: Ammoniacal silver
items.text: Make it fresh in the hood, use it once, never store, cap or let it dry: residues can become explosive.

items.title: Ammonia
items.text: Concentrated ammonia irritates eyes and airways: open and use it in the hood, titrating drop by drop.

items.title: Developer
items.text: Formaldehyde is a carcinogen and nitric acid is corrosive: make the developer in the hood, same day.

items.title: Gold chloride
items.text: Gloves, goggles and a lab coat for every reagent; read its safety data sheet before the first run.

items.title: Sodium thiosulfate
items.text: Gloves, goggles and a lab coat, as for every reagent; its safety data sheet is read before the first run.

items.title: Xylene (clearing)
items.text: Xylene is flammable and toxic to breathe: use it in the hood.

items.title: Silver waste
items.text: Nothing is poured away. Ammoniacal silver and developer go straight to the silver waste the EHS procedure names.

items.title: Silver waste container
items.text: Ammoniacal silver and developer go to the silver waste the EHS procedure names; the jar is rinsed the same hour.
